cards.text:
Place 1 power counter on Alix T4LB07 whenever you install a card.
[click],[trash]: Gain 2[credit] for each power counter on Alix T4LB07.
cards.title: Alix T4LB07

cards.text: When you install this program, you may spend any number of credits to place that many power counters on it. This program gets +1 strength for each hosted power counter, and it can only interface with ice of exactly equal strength. Interface → 1[credit]: Break 1 subroutine.
cards.title: Atman

cards.text: You can install bioroid ice onto this upgrade at no install cost. Whenever the Runner passes all of the ice protecting this server, you may rez 1 hosted piece of ice, paying 7[credit] less. If you do, the Runner encounters that ice. When this run ends, trash that ice.
cards.title: Awakening Center

cards.text: [subroutine] End the run.
cards.title: Bastion

cards.text: Rez a piece of bioroid ice, ignoring all costs, and install Bioroid Efficiency Research on that ice as a hosted condition counter with the text "Trash Bioroid Efficiency Research and derez host ice if all of its subroutines are broken during a single encounter."
cards.title: Bioroid Efficiency Research

cards.text:
+1[link]
Your maximum hand size is increased by 1.
cards.title: Borrowed Satellite

cards.text: Your maximum hand size is equal to the number of credits in your credit pool.
cards.title: Cerebral Imaging: Infinite Frontiers

cards.text:
You can advance this asset.
When the Runner accesses this asset while it is installed, you may pay 3[credit] to do X core damage. X is equal to the number of hosted advancement counters.
cards.title: Cerebral Overwriter

cards.text:
Whenever you make a successful run on R&D, place 1 virus counter on Chakana.
If there are at least 3 virus counters on Chakana, the advancement requirement of all agendas is increased by 1.
cards.title: Chakana

cards.text: 1[recurring-credit] Use this credit to pay for using icebreakers.
cards.title: Cloak

cards.text: [trash]: Install a program from your heap (paying the install cost).
cards.title: Clone Chip

cards.text: You cannot include Jinteki cards in this deck.
cards.title: Custom Biotics: Engineered for Success

cards.text: When you install this program, choose a server. Use this program only during runs on the chosen server. Interface → 1[credit]: Break 1 code gate subroutine. 1[credit]: +1 strength.
cards.title: Cyber-Cypher

cards.text: Interface → 1[credit]: Break 1 sentry subroutine. 1[credit]: +5 strength. Spend credits only from stealth cards to use this ability.
cards.title: Dagger

cards.text:
When you install this resource, load 8[credit] onto it. When it is empty, trash it.
When your turn begins, take 2[credit] from this resource.
cards.title: Daily Casts

cards.text:
[subroutine] The Runner must pay 2[credit], if able. If the Runner cannot pay 2[credit], end the run.
[subroutine] End the run.
cards.title: Datapike

cards.text:
You get +1 allotted [click] for each of your turns.
When this asset is trashed from anywhere while being accessed, add it to the Runner's score area as an agenda worth 2 agenda points.
cards.title: Director Haas

cards.text:
When you score this agenda, you may create a new remote server by installing up to 3 cards from HQ and/or Archives in the root of and/or protecting that server, ignoring all install costs.
Limit 1 per deck.
cards.title: Director Haas' Pet Project

cards.text: Run any server. When that run ends, if it was successful, gain 5[credit].
cards.title: Dirty Laundry

cards.text: Place 3 agenda counters on Efficiency Committee when you score it. [click], hosted agenda counter: Gain [click][click]. You cannot advance cards for the remainder of this turn.
cards.title: Efficiency Committee

cards.text: Run HQ. If successful, instead of breaching HQ, rearrange any number of ice protecting all servers. (Do not rez or derez any ice or change the number of ice protecting any server.)
cards.title: Escher

cards.text: Whenever you install a program from your heap, draw 1 card.
cards.title: Exile: Streethawk

cards.text: Run any server. If successful, instead of breaching that server, remove up to 3 advancement counters from 1 card in the root of or protecting the attacked server.
cards.title: Exploratory Romp

cards.text: [interrupt] → 3[credit]: Prevent 1 net damage. [interrupt] → [trash]: Prevent up to 2 core damage.
cards.title: Feedback Filter

cards.text: Trash up to 5 programs from your grip. Gain 2[credit] for each program trashed.
cards.title: Freelance Coding Contract

cards.text: [click], [click]: Gain 3[credit].
cards.title: Gila Hands Arcology

cards.text: You can advance this asset if it is unrezzed. Once per turn → [click], hosted advancement counter: Gain [click][click].
cards.title: Haas Arcology AI

cards.text: Lose [click][click]: Break up to 2 subroutines on this ice. Only the Runner can use this ability. [subroutine] Do 1 core damage. [subroutine] Do 1 core damage and end the run. [subroutine] End the run.
cards.title: Heimdall 2.0

cards.text: [subroutine] You may install and rez 1 piece of bioroid ice from HQ or Archives directly inward from this ice, ignoring all costs. When this run ends, if you installed a piece of ice this way, trash this ice and derez the ice you installed.
cards.title: Howler

cards.text:
Whenever the Corp rezzes a piece of ice, place 1[credit] on Ice Analyzer.
You may use credits on Ice Analyzer to install programs.
cards.title: Ice Analyzer

cards.text: Lose [click][click]: Break up to 2 subroutines on this ice. Only the Runner can use this ability. [subroutine] Trash 1 installed program. [subroutine] Trash 1 installed program. [subroutine] Trace[3]. If successful, do 1 core damage and give the Runner 1 tag.
cards.title: Ichi 2.0

cards.text: Interface → 1[credit]: Break 1 barrier subroutine. 2[credit]: +1 strength for the remainder of this run.
cards.title: Inti

cards.text: Shuffle your grip and heap into your stack. Draw 5 cards. Remove Levy AR Lab Access from the game instead of trashing it.
cards.title: Levy AR Lab Access

cards.text: [click], 1[credit]: Search R&D for a piece of ice, reveal it, and add it to HQ. Shuffle R&D.
cards.title: Levy University

cards.text: [subroutine] You may install 1 piece of ice from HQ protecting this server, ignoring the install cost.
cards.title: Minelayer

cards.text: +3[mu] When you install this hardware, install up to 3 programs from your grip, paying 4[credit] less for each. [interrupt] → Trash 1 program from your grip: Prevent 1 core damage or 1 net damage. Limit 1 console per player.
cards.title: Monolith

cards.text: Before taking your first turn, you may install up to 3 pieces of ice, with no more than a single piece of ice per server. Draw until you have 5 cards in HQ.
cards.title: NEXT Design: Guarding the Net

cards.text:
Omni-drive can host a single program of 1[mu] or less. The memory cost of the hosted program does not count against your memory limit.
1[recurring-credit]
Use this credit to pay for using the hosted program.
cards.title: Omni-drive

cards.text: 2[recurring-credit] (When you install this card and before your turn begins, refill to 2 hosted credits.) You can spend hosted credits to pay trash costs of assets.
cards.title: Paricia

cards.text: [click]: Gain 1[credit] and draw 1 card.
cards.title: Professional Contacts

cards.text: When you score this agenda, place 3 agenda counters on it. Hosted agenda counter: The rezzed piece of bioroid ice the Runner is approaching gains "[subroutine] End the run." after its other subroutines for the remainder of this run.
cards.title: Project Wotan

cards.text: The first time each turn you encounter a piece of ice, it gains code gate for the remainder of this run.
cards.title: Rielle “Kit” Peddler: Transhuman

cards.text:
2[recurring-credit]
Use these credits to install programs (you cannot use Sahasrara to install a program that trashes Sahasrara).
cards.title: Sahasrara

cards.text: [click], [click], [trash]: Play an event from your heap (paying its play cost).
cards.title: Same Old Thing

cards.text:
As an additional cost to play this event, trash 1 installed program.
 Install 1 program from your grip or heap, paying X[credit] less. X is equal to the install cost of the program you trashed.
cards.title: Scavenge

cards.text: 2[credit], [trash]: Search your stack for 1 program. Install it. (Shuffle your stack after searching it.)
cards.title: Self-modifying Code

cards.text: Whenever the Runner suffers at least 1 core damage, do 1 net damage.
cards.title: Sentinel Defense Program

cards.text:
Gain 2[credit] when your turn begins.
Trash Server Diagnostics when you install a piece of ice.
cards.title: Server Diagnostics

cards.text:
Play only if the Runner made an unsuccessful run during their last turn.
Gain 7[credit].
cards.title: Successful Demonstration

cards.text: The first copy of each program in this deck does not count against your influence limit.
cards.title: The Professor: Keeper of Knowledge

cards.text:
The advancement requirement of all agendas is increased by 1.
As an additional cost to steal an agenda, you must pay 3[credit].
Trash The Source when an agenda is scored or stolen.
cards.title: The Source

cards.text:
Thomas Haas can be advanced.
[trash]: Gain 2[credit] for each advancement token on Thomas Haas.
cards.title: Thomas Haas

cards.text: [interrupt] → When a subroutine would be broken on a piece of bioroid ice protecting this server, you may rez this upgrade. [interrupt] → [trash]: Prevent 1 subroutine from being broken on a piece of bioroid ice protecting this server.
cards.title: Tyr's Hand

cards.text: Lose [click][click]: Break up to 2 subroutines on this ice. Only the Runner can use this ability. Hosted power counter: Do 1 core damage. [subroutine] Trace[2]. If successful, place 1 power counter on this ice. [subroutine] End the run.
cards.title: Viktor 2.0

cards.text: Lose [click]: Break 1 subroutine on this ice. Only the Runner can use this ability. [subroutine] If the Runner has lost [click] to break a subroutine during this run, do 1 core damage. [subroutine] If the Runner has lost [click] to break a subroutine during this run, do 1 core damage.
cards.title: Zed 1.0

printings.flavor: The densest information cluster in the galaxy.
The Once and Future Android.
"Why limit our best assets to our own servers? The enemy doesn't stay passively at home, waiting for us to come to him. Why should we?" -Director Haas
The Alix model was based on a successful hedge fund manager but she had a tendency to burn out. Literally.
Thomas, the director's son, has been carefully groomed to inherit the corporation since before he was born. His favorite pastime appears to be disappointing his mother.
Success is defined by the safety of data, not the safety of potential intruders.
The realm beyond is still forbidden.
"Yeah. It made a loud noise, I got scared, and I jacked out. I still think I made the right decision." -g00ru
The game has changed.
Sometimes you just have to guess.
A mind of meat! How does it work?
Sell the dream-show them how very much they want to be rich, and they'll convince themselves that someday, they will be. How can they revolt against their future selves? -the New Gospel of Wealth
"Just another factory, making good corporate drones for the machine. Their CS department is the best in the world, though." -g00ru
"There's only a 5% chance this could result in a general failure."

The principle behind ice is not to keep everyone out, but to let only some people in. This ice denies entry on all but a select few ports that might change with the time of day or picosecond of connection. If you don't know what port to use, you're not getting in. Period.
"Cheap, off-the-shelf data protection. Cheap for them, that is. Not for us." -Ele "Smoke" Scovak
"I was not; I was; I am not; I am all."
"New technology destroys the old."
"I can make that work."
Wheeeee!
"Idealism's great, but it don't keep you in soybeef tacos." -Matt "TheMerc" Thomas
One man's trash.
Spend too much time in the AR Lab and someone might notice. Unless you're the head of it, that is.
It still hurts, a bit, the first time. The second time, you feel nothing at all. But don't push your luck.
It is good practice to backup the backup.
We are shaped by our thoughts; we become what we think.
"No line that they lay could catch a shadow on the wall…"
"…and once the shadow rises, the curtain shall fall." -revenant
Perfect for flooding servers.

"Make sure you tell the source code which executable you want it to compile into. One time I left my rig for a couple of minutes, and when I came back all of my files had been replaced with cat vids." -The Professor
Out there, the thousand-petaled lotus symbolizes detachment from illusion. In here, it is the birthplace of a higher consciousness. Something infinitely pure.
"The Incans believed that the sun god resided in the Haman Pacha, the upper realm of the cosmos. They just didn't know that the Haman Pacha hadn't been discovered yet." -The Professor
Sometimes it doesn't matter how expensive your rig is, or how many credits are in your account, or even your skill as a runner. Most of the time, a simple handshake and a name are all you need.
Some people have their own satellite receiver. Others have their own satellite.
"If you know the source code you can write to beat it, or just rejigger it a little and make it yours. That works, too." -Exile
The data was better than she could have ever imagined. This Santiago fellow really knew what he was doing. She began to imagine the havoc she could wreak at the upcoming charity dinner…
"We say 'cyber-terrorist', they hear 'underground celebrity.'" -Michael Muhama, professional expert
Just me, a cup of YucaBean, and last night's Hong Kong Trunk sniffed packets. I call that a good morning.
A dangerous game, but well worth playing.
